title: fix(runtime): a declarative update action refuses a caller with no edit grant 403 before the record lookup, as the data door does
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DEFxACyPwHxUwJy1F7vBLFD)_

domain:server#1 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czxVZYV4CcMiCbofw3

Fixes #30848

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

Claim: comment 6679693194 (branch `claude/project-thread-y8qx4d`).

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：声明式更新动作（`operation: 'update'`，REST `/actions` 与 MCP `run_action`）在按"读不到这条记录"回 404 之前，先问调用者对该对象有没有编辑权；没有就回 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`，与数据接口（`PATCH /data`、MCP `update_record`）对同一次写入的回答一致。
- 为什么改：只读无编辑权的用户改一条看不到的记录（或不存在的 id），动作门答 404、数据门答 403，同一次写入两个答案；文档写明"拒绝先于记录查找"、声明式更新"与用户编辑完全一致"。场景卡 #30802 因此无法写出唯一的预期拒绝。
- 风险与回滚：只在记录加载被拒时多问一次安全服务的 `explain(update)`，正常路径不变；有编辑权的人仍对"看不到的行"和"不存在的 id"回同一个 404，不形成存在性探测。单 PR 可整体回滚。
- 先看：`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`（`refuseUngrantedDeclarativeUpdate` 与 `executeDeclarativeUpdateAction` 中它的调用点）、`packages/runtime/src/declarative-update-refusal-order.pin.test.ts`。
- 两分钟验证：`cd packages/runtime && pnpm exec vitest run --project local src/declarative-update-refusal-order.pin.test.ts`，预期 20/20 通过。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

- New `refuseUngrantedDeclarativeUpdate` in `@objectstack/runtime` (`action-execution.ts`). `executeDeclarativeUpdateAction`, the executor both action doors call (REST `/actions` and MCP `run_action`), now calls it before it consumes the subject-load verdict (`refuseDeniedSubjectLoad`), and only when that load was denied.
- The ask is the security service's `explain({ object, operation: 'update' })`, the contract's "would the middleware allow this operation?" answer, computed by the enforcement walk. The REST import-template gate already asks `create` the same way. No row is named in the ask, so the answer cannot depend on whether the id names a row. Nothing is re-derived from permission sets, and nothing changes in `plugin-security`.
- A denial, or an `explain` that throws, refuses with the data door's own refusal: `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` with the middleware's user-facing sentence (`permission_denied` via `renderOperationMessage`, the caller's locale, the deployment's i18n override). With no security service, or one without `explain`, nothing is refused here, as at the data door.
- A delivered row is unchanged: the write that follows carries the caller's identity and the data plane answers its own 403. A caller who may update the object keeps the not-found answer, one answer for a hidden row and a missing id.
- Docblocks on `executeDeclarativeUpdateAction` updated to name the new order.

### The line the card asked for

On `main` `a2f523aa`, `invokeBusinessAction` loads the subject at `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts:4406` (`const subject = await loadActionSubjectRecord(…)`), and the declarative branch refuses on that load's verdict at `:4169` (`refuseDeniedSubjectLoad(objectName, recordId, subject)` in `executeDeclarativeUpdateAction`) before the write, the one place the object-level edit permission was asked, is attempted. The REST `/actions` door follows the same sequence (`domains/actions.ts`, its own load, then the same executor).

### Other subject-loading paths (checked, not changed)

- There is no declarative delete: `ActionSchema.operation` is `z.enum(['update'])`.
- The other `refuseDeniedSubjectLoad` callers are read admissions, not writes performed as the caller: the flow and script/body dispatch (`refuseDeniedSubjectLoadBeforeDispatch`), the api forward that needs the row, and the flow start record keys (`refuseUnreadableFlowStartRecords`). No data door performs the same write for the same caller, so there is no second answer to disagree with. Their 404 is the read-admission answer by design (#15079, #16370). They do not share this bug, and no follow-up is listed.

## Why

`content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx`, "Refusals come before the record lookup": a caller who may not update the object gets the same 403 whether or not the record id names a record. `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx`: a declarative update fires with the caller's permissions "exactly as for a user edit". Both sentences were false for the action door. The finding came from #30802 / PR #30846 (`travel_expense` op 4), which needs one expected refusal for this operation.

## Tests

`packages/runtime/src/declarative-update-refusal-order.pin.test.ts` boots one kernel (the plugin set `unresolved-object-name.actions-door.pin.test.ts` uses: ObjectQL, sqlite-wasm, Hono, the app, platform objects, auth, security, sharing, REST, dispatcher). Object `pin_step` is private OWD with a declarative `decide` action. Two invited members: a reader (default set: read + create) and an editor (an assigned set: read + create + edit). Each member owns one row.

- Matrix: {reader, editor} × {own row, the other member's row, a missing id} × four doors: `PATCH /data`, the MCP bridge's `update` (what `update_record` calls), `POST /actions/pin_step/decide/:id`, and the MCP bridge's `runAction` (what `run_action` calls). The MCP leg is driven through the real `/mcp` route with a stand-in `mcp` service that calls the two bridge members and reports the thrown `status` and `code`. The tools' own envelope rendering is `@objectstack/mcp`'s and is not under test here. Expected: the reader gets 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` on all three rows at every door; the editor gets 200 on its own row and 404 `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` on the other two at every door. A refused write leaves the row untouched.
- Existence-oracle equality: within each door and for each caller, the hidden row and the missing id get the same answer, body included, once the id is written out (8 cases). For the reader, the visible row's refusal at each door is that same answer too, sentence included (4 cases). So the action door's 403 carries the data plane's sentence.
- Preconditions: each member reads its own row and gets 404 on the other's; the administrator reads both.

<details><summary>Baseline on main's action door (the re-measure)</summary>

The pin run against `origin/main`'s `action-execution.ts` (test file kept): 2 failed / 14 passed of the first 16 cases. Both failures were reader × hidden row and reader × missing id, at exactly two doors:

```
  "action MCP":  expected { code: PERMISSION_DENIED, status: 403 }  received { code: RECORD_NOT_FOUND, status: 404 }
  "action REST": expected { code: PERMISSION_DENIED, status: 403 }  received { code: RECORD_NOT_FOUND, status: 404 }
  "data MCP":    { code: PERMISSION_DENIED, status: 403 }   (as expected)
```

Every other cell, including editor × hidden/missing (404 at all doors) and both visible rows, already agreed. This is the card's table (filer's probe on `c17719dd`) on current main. The filer's probe script needs PR #30846's scenario harness worktree, so the re-measure went through this booted pin instead.

</details>

<details><summary>Ablation (restored: blob equals HEAD, git diff HEAD empty)</summary>

- Mutation via `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the verdict is consumed before the ask (`refuseDeniedSubjectLoad(…); await refuseUngrantedDeclarativeUpdate(…)`), i.e. the old order. The anchor went 1 → 0, and the blob went `97cc3fe3` → `7e1ef3a8`. The suite imports runtime `src/` directly, so no dist rebuild is needed.
- Result: 4 failed / 16 passed. Reader × hidden and reader × missing are red in the matrix, and the reader's visible-vs-missing equality is red at `action REST` and `action MCP`. Every editor row and every data-door row stays green.
- Restore: blob after restore `97cc3fe3` equals HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- The first ablation attempt was a no-op and is not counted: its replacement still contained the anchor, so `ablation-replace` refused before running anything (anchor 1 → 1). The second attempt is the reading above.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- The ask is object-level `update` with no payload, so two pre-lookup refusals the data door gives a caller who holds the update grant are not asked here: a field-level write refusal on a field the payload names (middleware step 2.5), and a read-only external datasource's write guard. For such a caller writing a hidden row or a missing id, the action door still answers 404 where the data door answers 403. Both answers stay the same for the hidden row and the missing id, so there is no oracle. This is not measured here, and the pinned matrix does not reach it.
- A caller whose read of the object is refused but who holds edit: the data door answers the read refusal. The action door asks only `update`, so it keeps 404 for that caller. This is not measured here, and it needs a permission set granting edit without read.
- `explain` denies a caller whose permission sets resolve empty. Since ADR-0056 D2 the middleware's CRUD gate does too, so this matches.

## Verification

All on head `2dc4bdfa`, except where a line names `ad748b98`. That earlier head differs only in docblocks and the changeset prose, plus one line removed from the new function: the `isSystem` short-circuit, dropped so that `explain` answers a system context as the middleware does.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`: exit 0 (2dc4bdfa).
- Focused: the new pin plus `action-declarative-update.test.ts`, `action-invocation-audit.test.ts` and `action-declarative-update-stale-summary.test.ts`: 4 files, 90 tests passed (2dc4bdfa).
- `@objectstack/runtime` local project, whole suite: 550 files, 8801 passed, 19 skipped (ad748b98).
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: 60 families, all run on 2dc4bdfa with exit 0; `--ran` reconciliation: 60 derived, 60 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED. The first pass on ad748b98 had one red, `check:system-context-census` (a new `isSystem` read in a symbol no census row names), cleared by dropping that line. It also had one exit 3, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (PREREQUISITE NOT MET, no whole-tree dist), which exits 0 on 2dc4bdfa.
- `pnpm lint`: exit 0 (2dc4bdfa).
- Changeset: `@objectstack/runtime` patch, carrying both declaration lines.
- Head `5f17e7c8` (one commit on `2dc4bdfa`, test-only): the merge queue's Dogfood Regression Gate (3/3) caught `showcase-anonymous-deny-surfaces.dogfood.test.ts` pinning the old 404 for the no-edit member (run 42192137004). The case now asserts this PR's 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` for the member, keeps #7867's ghost-id 404 with the dev administrator who holds the edit grant, and compares the action with the PATCH for both callers. Dogfood, full suite unsharded on `5f17e7c8`: 423 files passed and 1 failed, 3537 tests passed and 2 failed. Both failures were `catalog-activation-door.dogfood.test.ts` :149 and :167 timing out at 5000 ms under box load; that file passed 10/10 alone on the same head, and the fixed file passed 80/80.

## Human Minimum

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic. (not touched)
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes.
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request.
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: not touched.
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English.
- [x] The *Before Submitting* list in CONTRIBUTING.md is done.
